elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section (a) grants this right, but Section (c) still prohibits any Licensee assignment without Licensor's prior written consent. The Change-of-Control exception in Section (c) does not generally cover affiliate assignments, so the operative provisions conflict.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section (a) expressly permits assignment without Licensor's consent to a successor in a merger. A merger involving a successor is also covered by the Change-of-Control definition and therefore by Section (c)'s direction that Change-of-Control transactions are governed by Section (a).

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section (a) expressly permits assignment without Licensor's consent to a successor in an acquisition; qualifying control acquisitions are also covered by the Change-of-Control provisions that Section (c) makes controlling.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Section (a) expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in a sale of all or substantially all assets, and that transaction is expressly included in the Change-of-Control definition.

elements.element: Vendor may assign only with Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause regulates Licensee assignments but imposes no Customer-consent requirement on assignments by Licensor.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires Customer to act reasonably regarding a proposed Licensor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor, even with Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: There is no restriction on Licensor assigning to a Licensee competitor. The remaining competitor language concerns Licensor's purported consent to Licensee's Change of Control, not Licensor's own assignments.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's Change of Control.
elements.evidence: Section (a) expressly provides that no Change of Control of Licensee shall terminate the Agreement or give Licensor any right to terminate it. The remaining consent sentence is dangling and inconsistent, but does not expressly restore a termination right.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (a) expressly permits Licensee to assign without Licensor's consent to a successor in a merger, consolidation, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no written-notice requirement for Licensee's assignment to a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: No operative provision grants Licensor a right to assign to a successor. The statement that the Agreement binds and benefits successors and permitted assigns does not itself authorize assignment.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation applies to a Licensor assignment to a successor.

elements.element: Other Customer assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (c) generally requires Licensor's prior written consent, but Section (a) separately permits affiliate assignments without consent. Because an affiliate assignment need not be a successor assignment, the required consent rule for all other assignments is not consistently operative.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Customer assignments.
elements.evidence: No operative reasonableness standard applies to Licensor's consent under Section (c). The remaining sentence deeming consent reasonably withheld concerns Change of Control and is not a general non-withholding obligation.

elements.element: Other Vendor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no Customer-consent requirement on Licensor's other assignments.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Vendor assignments.
elements.evidence: No operative language addresses Customer consent to, or unreasonable withholding of consent for, Licensor assignments.

result.reason: Neither position is fully achieved. The affiliate carve-out conflicts with the unchanged assignment prohibition, and all required Vendor-assignment protections are omitted. The fallback also lacks mutual successor rights and notice obligations, as well as bilateral reasonableness standards. The draft leaves obsolete consent language in the Change-of-Control section and adds unrequested suspension and repricing restrictions, creating ambiguity and exceeding the changes needed for the stated assignment rule.
